text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said in Washington that Poland wants to take part in reducing the debt of the world's poorest countries. NBP President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the IMF asked Poland to help sort out Bulgaria's banking crisis.

The Economic Development Institute of the Warsaw School of Economics (SGH) said its monthly industrial climate indicator rose three points in September to nine points, with firms reporting higher production, more domestic and foreign orders, and an improvement in their financial situations. NOWA EUROPA
The Dutch capital group Fortis and Polish banks BGZ and Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej want to take over the Katowice- based Feniks insurer, as does German insurance holding Allianz.
Transport ministers from the European Union countries decided to start talks with 10 Central and Eastern European countries on gradual cooperation on air transport routes. GAZETA WYBORCZA

Several insurance firms are in poor financial stead, the head of the insurance inspection office said, adding that the weaker firms could soon collapse and that consolidation was difficult because no insurers possessed the money that banks do.
Ruch, Poland's largest press distributor, is slowly losing market share as its privatisation process drags on. Negotiations with French-Polish Hachette-SPC should last about another two weeks.
Central bank adviser Jan Krzysztof Solorz said Polish banks would be able to boost lending if they combined their capital with that of insurance firms.
